newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: DUTCH DOUWE EGBERTS HOLDS COFFEE PRICE "FOR NOW".
newsitem.headline: DUTCH DOUWE EGBERTS HOLDS COFFEE PRICE "FOR NOW".

text.p: Douwe Egberts, the leading coffee roaster in the Netherlands, said on Wednesday it had no plans to increase retail prices but could not rule out a further rise in the near future.

"We are not translating these higher world prices into an increase in shop prices at the moment but we will do if it impacts on our costs," said Joost den Haan, spokesman for Douwe Egberts, owned by U.S. giant Sara Lee Corp .
A week ago, the company raised the Dutch price of a standard 250-gramme pack of coffee by 20 cents, making it retail at an average of four guilders, the third price rise this year.
World raw coffee prices have spiralled higher this year on concerns over Latin American supplies and tight consumer stocks.

The focus has been mostly on supplies of the premium arabica bean grown in Latin America and traded in New York. Prices of the robusta variety, used mostly to make instant coffee, have lagged a little, but even these are now at year-highs in London.
Douwe Egberts said it had not and would not alter the proportion of arabica and robusta beans used in its blends.
"We are a premium brand and the most important thing is to maintain the quality of our product," Den Haan said.
